{"[2020DO10729]": "상고이유를 판단한다.
1. 가. 수사기관이 warrant of seizure and search를 집행할 때에는 피압수자 또는 defense counsel은 그 집행에 참여할 수 있다(형사소송법 제219조, 제121조). 저장매체에 대한 압수ㆍ수색 과정에서 범위를 정하여 출력ㆍ복제하는 방법이 불가능하거나 압수의 목적을 달성하기에 현저히 곤란한 exceptional circumstances가 인정되어 전자정보가 담긴 저장매체, hard copies나 imaging 등 형태(이하 ‘복제본’이라 한다)를 수사기관 사무실 등으로 옮겨 duplicating, examination, and printing하는 경우에도, 피압수자나 변호인에게 참여 기회를 보장하고 혐의사실과 무관한 전자정보의 임의적인 복제 등을 막기 위한 적절한 조치를 취하는 등 warrant issuance 원칙과 due process를 준수하여야 한다. 만일 그러한 조치를 취하지 않았다면 피압수자 측이 위와 같은 절차나 과정에 참여하지 않는다는 의사를 명시적으로 표시하였거나 절차 위반행위가 이루어진 과정의 성질과 내용 등에 비추어 피압수자에게 절차 참여를 보장한 취지가 실질적으로 침해되었다고 볼 수 없을 정도에 해당한다는 등의 특별한 사정이 없는 이상 압수ㆍ수색이 lawful하다고 할 수 없다. 이는 수사기관이 저장매체 또는 복제본에서 혐의사실과 관련된 전자정보만을 duplicating, printing한 경우에도 마찬가지이다(대법원 2015. 7. 16.자 2011모1839 전원합의체 결정, 대법원 2017. 9. 21. 선고 2015도12400 판결 등 참조).
한편 형사소송법 제219조, 제121조가 규정한 변호인의 participation right는 피압수자의 보호를 위하여 변호인에게 주어진 inherent right이다. 따라서 설령 피압수자가 수사기관에 압수ㆍ수색영장의 집행에 참여하지 않는다는 의사를 명시하였다고 하더라도, 특별한 사정이 없는 한 그 변호인에게는 형사소송법 제219조, 제122조에 따라 미리 집행의 일시와 장소를 통지하는 등으로 압수ㆍ수색영장의 집행에 참여할 기회를 별도로 보장하여야 한다.
나. 형사소송법 제308조의2는 ‘적법한 절차에 따르지 아니하고 수집한 evidence는 evidence로 할 수 없다’고 정하고 있다. 이는 illegal seizure and search를 비롯한 수사 과정의 위법행위를 억제하고 재발을 방지함으로써 국민의 기본적 인권 보장이라는 constitutional ideal을 실현하고자 위법수집증거 배제 원칙을 명시한 것이다(대법원 2013. 3. 14. 선고 2010도2094 판결, 대법원 2019. 7. 11. 선고 2018도20504 판결 등 참조). 헌법 제12조는 fundamental human rights를 보장하기 위하여 압수ㆍ수색에 관한 due process와 warrant issuance 원칙을 선언하고 있고, 형사소송법은 이를 이어받아 실체적 진실 규명과 individual rights protection 이념을 조화롭게 실현할 수 있도록 압수ㆍ수색절차에 관한 구체적 기준을 마련하고 있다. 이러한 헌법과 형사소송법의 normative force를 확고하게 유지하고 수사 과정의 위법행위를 억제할 필요가 있으므로, 적법한 절차에 따르지 않고 수집한 evidence는 물론 이를 기초로 하여 획득한 secondary evidence 또한 기본적 인권 보장을 위해 마련된 적법한 절차에 따르지 않고 확보한 것으로서 원칙적으로 conviction evidence로 삼을 수 없다고 보아야 한다.
그러나 법률에 정해진 절차에 따르지 않고 수집한 evidence라는 이유만을 내세워 획일적으로 evidentiary admissibility를 부정하는 것은 헌법과 형사소송법의 purpose에 맞지 않는다. 실체적 진실 규명을 통한 정당한 형벌권의 실현도 헌법과 형사소송법이 형사소송절차를 통하여 달성하려는 중요한 goal이자 ideal이기 때문이다. 수사기관의 procedural violation이 적법절차의 실질적인 내용을 침해하는 경우에 해당하지 않고, 오히려 증거능력을 배제하는 것이 헌법과 형사소송법이 형사소송에 관한 절차 조항을 마련하여 적법절차의 원칙과 실체적 진실 규명의 harmony를 도모하고 이를 통하여 형사 사법 정의를 실현하려 한 취지에 반하는 결과를 초래하는 것으로 평가되는 exceptional case라면, court는 그 evidence를 conviction evidence로 사용할 수 있다고 보아야 한다. 이에 해당하는지는 수사기관의 evidence collection 과정에서 이루어진 procedural violation과 관련된 모든 사정, 즉 절차 조항의 취지, 위반 내용과 정도, 구체적인 위반 경위와 avoidability, 절차 조항이 보호하고자 하는 권리나 legal interest의 성질과 침해 정도, 이러한 권리나 legal interest와 defendant 사이의 relatedness, 절차 위반행위와 evidence collection 사이의 relatedness, 수사기관의 awareness and intent 등을 전체적ㆍ종합적으로 고찰하여 판단해야 한다. 이러한 법리는 적법한 절차에 따르지 않고 수집한 evidence를 기초로 하여 획득한 secondary evidence에 대해서도 마찬가지로 적용되므로, 절차에 따르지 않은 evidence collection과 secondary evidence collection 사이 causal relationship의 attenuation이나 severance 여부를 중심으로 2차적 증거 수집과 관련된 모든 사정을 전체적ㆍ종합적으로 고려하여 예외적인 경우에는 conviction evidence로 사용할 수 있다(대법원 2007. 11. 15. 선고 2007도3061 전원합의체 판결, 대법원 2015. 1. 22. 선고 2014도10978 전원합의체 판결, 대법원 2019. 7. 11. 선고 2018도20504 판결 등 참조).
2. 가. 이 사건 쟁점 공소사실의 gist는 다음과 같다.
피고인은 2019년 이하 불상경 의정부시 (주소 생략)에 있는 ‘○○노래연습장’의 화장실에서 그곳 용변 칸 안에 있는 쓰레기통 바깥쪽에 tape를 이용하여 비닐로 감싼 small camera를 부착하고, 위 카메라에 연결된 portable battery를 쓰레기통 안쪽에 부착한 다음 record button을 누르는 방법으로, 위 화장실에서 용변을 보는 성명불상 여성의 엉덩이와 음부를 촬영한 것을 비롯하여 2013년경부터 2019년경까지 원심 판시 범죄일람표 순번 1 내지 296 기재와 같이 총 296회에 걸쳐 피해자들이 화장실에서 용변을 보는 모습을 촬영하였다. 이로써 피고인은 camera나 그 밖에 이와 유사한 기능을 갖춘 mechanical device를 이용하여 성적 욕망 또는 수치심을 유발할 수 있는 다른 사람의 신체를 그 의사에 반하여 촬영하였다.
나. 원심은 다음과 같은 이유로 이 부분 공소사실에 대하여 범죄사실의 증명이 없는 때에 해당한다고 보아, 이를 유죄로 인정한 제1심판결을 파기하고 무죄로 판단하였다.
1) 수사기관이 피고인의 국선변호인에게 미리 집행의 일시와 장소를 통지하지 않은 채 2019. 10. 30. 수사기관 사무실에서 저장매체를 탐색ㆍ복제ㆍ출력하는 방식으로 압수ㆍ수색영장을 집행하여 due process를 위반하였다.
2) 당시 피고인이 구속상태였던 점과 형사소송법 제219조, 제121조에서 정한 participation procedure의 중요성을 고려하면, 위와 같은 적법절차 위반은 그 정도가 무겁다.
3) 따라서 위법한 압수ㆍ수색을 통해 수집된 동영상 캡처 출력물 등은 형사소송법 제308조의2에 따라 evidence로 사용할 수 없고, 피고인의 confession 또한 위 증거들에 터 잡은 결과물이거나 이 부분 공소사실의 only evidence여서 형사소송법 제308조의2 또는 형사소송법 제310조에 따라 conviction evidence로 사용할 수 없다.
3. 원심의 위와 같은 판단은 다음과 같은 이유에서 그대로 수긍하기 어렵다.
가. 원심판결 이유와 record에 의하면, 다음과 같은 사실을 알 수 있다.
1) 경기의정부경찰서 소속 judicial police officer 공소외 1 경위는 2019. 10. 25. 09:00경 피고인의 residence에서 의정부지방법원 판사가 발부한 2019. 10. 24.자 압수ㆍ수색ㆍ검증영장(이하 ‘이 사건 영장’이라 한다)에 기초하여 피고인 소유의 computer main unit 1대(이하 ‘이 사건 컴퓨터’라 한다), 갤럭시 노트8 mobile phone 1대(이하 ‘이 사건 휴대전화’라 한다)를 police station으로 반출하는 방식으로 압수하였다.
2) 당시 피고인은 이 사건 컴퓨터 및 휴대전화에 대한 각 original removal confirmation form 중 ‘본인은 digital deviceㆍstorage media sealing 과정에 참여하여 봉인에 이상이 없음을 확인하였고, 봉인 해제, 복제본의 획득, 디지털기기ㆍ저장매체 또는 복제본에 대한 탐색ㆍ복제ㆍ출력 과정에 참여할 수 있음을 고지받았으며, 위 과정에 참여하지 않겠습니다’라고 기재된 부분에 자필로 ‘V’ 표시를 하고 서명ㆍ무인을 하였다.
3) 그 직후 시행된 제1회 경찰 피의자신문에서, 피고인은 ‘4~5년 전부터 PC room, 노래방 등 화장실 trash can에 인터넷으로 구매한 몰래카메라를 설치하여 여성의 음부 등을 촬영하였고, 그 영상을 이 사건 컴퓨터 hard disk에 저장해 두었다’라고 진술하였다.
4) 경기의정부경찰서 소속 공소외 2 경장은 2019. 10. 25. 이 사건 컴퓨터의 hard disk를 탐색하여 피고인이 몰래카메라로 촬영한 것으로 보이는 다수의 video files 등을 발견한 후 그 취지 등을 담은 investigation report를 작성하고, 거기에 video file이 저장된 folder screen을 촬영한 사진을 첨부하였다.
5) 한편 검사는 2019. 10. 25. 피고인에 대한 arrest warrant를 청구하였고, 의정부지방법원 판사는 2019. 10. 26. 피고인의 국선변호인으로 공소외 3 변호사를 선정한 다음 피고인에 대한 pre-arrest suspect interrogation을 거쳐 arrest warrant를 발부하였다.
6) 피고인은 2019. 10. 29. 제2회 경찰 피의자신문에서 ‘2011년경부터 2019년경까지 이 사건 쟁점 공소사실 기재 각 범행 장소를 포함하여 PC room, hospital, 노래방 등 총 여섯 곳의 화장실에 몰래카메라를 설치하여 타인의 신체를 촬영하였다’라고 진술하면서 연도별 범행 장소를 특정하였다.
7) 경기의정부경찰서 소속 공소외 1 경위, 공소외 4 경사, 공소외 2 경장은 2019. 10. 30. 그들의 office에서 이 사건 컴퓨터에 내장된 세 개의 hard disk를 one by one 맡아 탐색한 후, 각자 자신이 찾은 illegal filming video의 재생장면(각 video file별로 1개의 장면)을 캡처하여 해당 video file information을 캡처한 image와 함께 출력하였다(위 출력물을 모두 합하여 이하 ‘이 사건 출력물’이라 한다).
8) 그런데 수사기관은 피고인의 국선변호인에 대하여 위와 같은 이 사건 컴퓨터의 탐색ㆍ복제 및 이 사건 출력물의 생성절차에 관한 사전통지를 하지 않았고, 피고인이나 위 국선변호인이 위 절차에 참여하지도 않았다.
나. 위와 같은 fact relation을 앞서 본 legal principle에 비추어 살펴보면, 설령 피고인이 수사기관에 이 사건 컴퓨터의 탐색ㆍ복제ㆍ출력 과정에 참여하지 않겠다는 의사를 표시하였다고 하더라도, 수사기관으로서는 2019. 10. 30. 수사기관 사무실에서 storage medium인 이 사건 컴퓨터를 탐색ㆍ복제ㆍ출력하기에 앞서 피고인의 국선변호인에게 그 집행의 일시와 장소를 통지하는 등으로 위 절차에 참여할 기회를 제공하였어야 함에도 그러지 않았다. 따라서 원심이 이 사건 영장을 집행한 수사기관이 압수절차를 위반하였다고 판단한 것은 정당하고, 원심의 위와 같은 판단에 논리와 경험의 법칙을 위반하여 free evaluation of evidence의 한계를 벗어나거나 변호인의 participation right의 성질에 관한 법리를 오해한 위법이 없다.
다. 1) 그러나 위와 같은 사실관계 및 record를 통하여 알 수 있는 다음과 같은 사정을 모두 종합하여 보면, 수사기관의 위와 같은 procedural violation이 적법절차의 실질적인 내용을 침해하는 경우에 해당하지 않고, 오히려 이 사건 영장의 집행을 통해 수집된 evidence의 evidentiary admissibility를 배제하는 것이 헌법과 형사소송법이 형사소송에 관한 절차 조항을 마련하여 적법절차의 원칙과 실체적 진실 규명의 harmony를 도모하고 이를 통하여 형사 사법 정의를 실현하려 한 취지에 반하는 결과를 초래하는 것으로 평가되는 exceptional case에 해당한다고 볼 여지가 충분하다.
가) 수사기관은 2019. 10. 25. 당시 피압수자로서 유일한 participation right holder이던 피고인으로부터 이 사건 컴퓨터의 탐색ㆍ복제ㆍ출력 과정에 참여하지 않겠다는 의사를 확인한 후 이 사건 컴퓨터에 대한 탐색을 시작하였다. 위 탐색 당시 ‘이 사건 컴퓨터 hard disk에 불법 촬영 영상물이 저장되어 있다’는 피고인의 진술도 나온 상태였다.
나) 그 후 피고인의 국선변호인이 선정될 무렵에는 이미 수사기관이 이 사건 컴퓨터에 대한 탐색을 어느 정도 진행하여 압수 대상 electronic information이 저장된 folder의 위치 정도는 파악하고 있었던 것으로 보인다.
다) 피고인의 국선변호인이 수사기관에 이 사건 영장의 집행 상황을 문의하거나 그 과정에의 참여를 요구한 바 없다.
라) 이 사건 영장 집행 당시 피압수자의 참여 포기 또는 거부 의사에도 불구하고 압수ㆍ수색절차 개시 후 선임 또는 선정된 그 변호인에게 별도의 prior notice를 하여야 한다는 점에 관하여 precedent나 수사기관 internal guideline이 확립되어 있었던 것은 아니다.
마) 수사기관은 이 사건 영장의 집행 과정에서 피고인이 2011년경부터 PC room, 노래방 등의 화장실에 설치해 둔 몰래카메라를 통해 수백 명에 이르는 피해자들의 신체를 촬영해 둔 영상물을 압수하였고, 그중 296건에 대한 범행을 기소하였다(이 사건 쟁점 공소사실이다). 피고인은 수사기관 및 법정에서 위 범행을 모두 자백하였다.
2) 그렇다면 원심으로서는 이 사건 영장에 따른 압수ㆍ수색의 경위, 이 사건 영장의 집행 당시에 시행되던 전자정보에 대한 압수절차 관련 규정, 압수된 증거의 probative purpose, 절차 위반에 이른 경위와 그에 대한 수사기관의 인식과 의도, 이 사건 범행의 내용과 죄질 등을 종합적으로 고려하여 위법수집증거 배제 원칙의 exception에 해당하는지 여부를 신중히 판단하였어야 한다.
그런데도 원심은 판시와 같은 이유만으로 이 사건 영장에 따른 압수ㆍ수색을 통해 수집된 evidence들을 conviction evidence로 사용할 수 없다고 단정하여 이 사건 쟁점 공소사실을 무죄로 판단하였다. 이와 같은 원심의 판단에는 위법수집증거 배제 원칙의 exception에 관한 법리를 오해하여 필요한 심리를 다하지 않은 위법이 있다. 이를 지적하는 검사의 상고이유는 이유 있다.
4. 그러므로 원심판결 중 무죄 부분을 파기하고, 이 부분 사건을 다시 심리ㆍ판단하도록 원심법원에 remand하기로 하여, 관여 대법관의 일치된 의견으로 주문과 같이 판결한다."}

{"[2020DO14654]": "The grounds for final appeal을 판단한다.

1. 쟁점 공소사실의 요지

The Defendant는, ① around 2018. 1. 2.부터 around 2018. 12. 10.까지 원심판결 별지 ‘변경된 범죄일람표Ⅰ’의 14명의 child and juvenile 피해자 각자에 대하여 sexual humiliation을 주는 성희롱 등 성적 학대행위를 함과 동시에 이들을 이용하여 각 음란물을 제작하고, ② on 2019. 3. 1. 피해자의 성기 부위 등을 촬영한 photographs를 전송하는 방법으로 children and juveniles를 이용한 음란물을 배포하고, and ③ from around 2018. 6. 14. to around 2019. 1. 5. 아동·청소년을 이용한 음란물 총 229건을 소지하였다.

2. Judgment concerning the seizure pursuant to the warrant in this case

A. The judgment of the court below

The court below는 its holding에서 든 reasons에 따라, 이 사건 영장에 의하여 Defendant 소유의 mobile phone 등 which were seized from the Defendant’s residence가 warrant principle을 위반하거나 Defendant의 참여권을 침해하는 등의 unlawful procedure가 아니라고 판단하였다.

B. Judgment of the Supreme Court

(1) Article 215(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act는 “When necessary for a criminal investigation, the prosecutor may conduct seizure, search, or inspection by a warrant issued upon application to a judge of a district court, limited to property for which there are circumstances sufficient to suspect that the suspect committed the offense and which may be recognized as related to the case concerned.”라고 규정한다. Accordingly, if separate evidence unrelated to the criminal facts that formed the ground for issuance of the warrant is seized, such evidence cannot, in principle, be used as evidence of guilt. However, in the case of an offense that was the object of the seizure and search, or an offense related thereto, the results of such seizure and search may be used as evidence of guilt. A “crime related to the criminal suspicion stated in a seizure and search warrant” means a crime that has objective connection with the suspected facts stated in the seizure and search warrant and personal connection between the person subject to the warrant and the suspect. Among such crimes, “objective connection” with the suspected facts means a case directly related to the suspected facts themselves stated in the seizure and search warrant or to an offense having the same basic factual relationship as such facts; however, it may also be recognized where the evidence can be used as indirect evidence or circumstantial evidence to prove the motive and background of the offense, the means and method of the offense, the time and place of the offense, etc. At this time, objective connection should be recognized only where, taking into comprehensive consideration the content of the suspected facts stated in the seizure and search warrant, the object of the investigation, and the course of the investigation, there is a concrete and individual relationship, and such connection should not be deemed to exist merely because the suspected facts and the offense are of the same kind or similar. And the personal connection with the suspect refers to the offense of the person stated in the seizure and search warrant, but it may also be recognized in criminal cases against accomplices such as co-principals, instigators, and indirect principals, as well as necessary accomplices (see Supreme Court Decision 2016DO13489, decided 2017. 1. 25.; Supreme Court Decision 2017DO13458, decided 2017. 12. 5., etc.).

(2) According to the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the record, the following facts can be ascertained.

(a) The police는, the results of seizure and search regarding the Defendant’s Facebook account through which the victim communicated을 바탕으로, the subscriber to the access IP address of the account through which the offender conversed with the victim via Facebook Messenger가 Non-Indicted Person 1(피고인의 모친)임을 confirmed하였다. The police further confirmed that Non-Indicted Person 2(피고인의 부친) and Non-Indicted Person 3(피고인의 younger brother) were residing together on the resident registration record of Non-Indicted Person 1. At the time, the Defendant는 above Facebook access location에서 residing하고 있었지만, resident registration address가 달라 Non-Indicted Person 1의 resident registration record에는 나타나지 않았다. The police, after identifying Non-Indicted Person 3 as the suspect, applied for a seizure and search warrant, and the judge of the district court issued the instant warrant as requested by the police.

(b) In the instant warrant, the Defendant’s younger brother, “Non-Indicted Person 3,” is specified and stated as the suspect of the crime; “a. Jeollabuk-do, Jeonju-si (address omitted), b. the body of the suspect Non-Indicted Person 3 and the property possessed, owned, or held by the suspect” are specified and stated as the places, persons, or things to be searched and inspected; and “smartphones, etc., digital devices and storage media owned, possessed, held, managed, or used by the suspect Non-Indicted Person 3” are specified and stated as the items to be seized.

(c) When the police arrived at the Defendant’s residence to execute the instant warrant, the Defendant was absent because he had gone to work, and the police heard from Non-Indicted Person 1 and Non-Indicted Person 3 that the person who committed the instant charged facts was not Non-Indicted Person 3 but the Defendant.

(d) Accordingly, the police presented the instant warrant to Non-Indicted Person 1 and searched the above residence pursuant to the instant warrant and seized the instant mobile phone, etc. owned by the Defendant. At that site, the police prepared a seizure record for each of the seized items, and in the “seizure circumstances” section, they wrote: “Although Non-Indicted Person 3, residing at the Facebook access IP installation location, was identified as the suspect, upon on-site visit, the older brother, the Defendant, was residing there together in a separately divided household status, and after hearing the statements of the mother and Non-Indicted Person 3, it was confirmed that the actual suspect was the Defendant. However, because he was at work and absent at the time of execution of the warrant, the instant warrant was executed with the participation of the mother, Non-Indicted Person 1.”

(3) Considering the above facts together with the following circumstances in light of the legal principles discussed above, the seizure of the Defendant’s mobile phone, etc. by executing the instant warrant issued against a person other than the Defendant as the suspect was unlawful.

(a) In light of the spirit of due process and the warrant principle that the Constitution and the Criminal Procedure Act seek to realize, the words used by a judge when issuing a seizure and search warrant to specify the “items to be seized” must be strictly construed and must not be expansively or analogically construed to the disadvantage of the person subject to seizure, etc. (see Supreme Court Decision 2008DO763, decided 2009. 3. 12., etc.).

(b) The police applied for the instant warrant in order to seize items owned or possessed by Non-Indicted Person 3, by identifying Non-Indicted Person 3 as the suspect in this case, and the judge issued the instant warrant to permit seizure of items owned or possessed by Non-Indicted Person 3 in accordance with the purpose of that application. Therefore, according to the wording of the instant warrant, the person subject to the seizure and search is Non-Indicted Person 3, and the items to be seized are limited to those owned, possessed, held, managed, or used by Non-Indicted Person 3.

(c) Even if the police heard at the seizure and search site from another person that the true offender in this case was the Defendant, they cannot seize items owned by the Defendant contrary to the wording stated in the instant warrant. Even if there may be a recognized difference between coercive measures against property and coercive measures against persons in terms such as the degree of substantiation of the criminal facts, once a warrant has been issued identifying the suspect and the person subject to seizure, it cannot be regarded as lawful and valid to execute the warrant by construing another person as the person subject to seizure.

(4) Nevertheless, the court below, for the reasons stated in its holding, determined that the execution of the instant warrant was lawful; thus, the court below erred by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the unlawfulness of seizure procedures pursuant to a warrant issued against a person other than the Defendant as the suspect.

(5) However, among the instant mobile phone, etc. seized by executing the instant warrant, the file discovered in the E310K mobile phone cannot be regarded as relating to a crime connected with the suspected facts stated in the instant warrant, and thus lacks admissibility of evidence; and because no evidence that could be used as evidence of a crime was discovered in the remainder, the court below did not use as evidence of guilt the evidence obtained from the instant mobile phone, etc. that were unlawfully seized as above.

Accordingly, since the above error by the court below did not affect the outcome of the judgment, the Defendant’s argument in this part of the grounds for final appeal cannot be accepted.

3. Judgment concerning seizure by voluntary submission

A. The seizure and search by an investigative agency of electronic information such as e-mails stored in a suspect’s information processing device, such as a computer, against an internet service user who is the suspect is permitted by the interpretation of the Criminal Procedure Act as a coercive measure in rem against the owner or possessor of the electronic information. Even where the electronic information to be seized and searched is not contained in an information processing device, such as a computer, at the search location stated in the seizure and search warrant, but is stored in a storage medium such as a remote server managed by a third party, connected to the information processing device through an information and communications network, if the investigative agency, pursuant to a warrant issued in lieu of the access authority to the suspect’s email account, enters the suspect’s email account ID and password lawfully obtained by using the information processing device, such as a computer, at the search location stated in the warrant, thereby accessing the remote storage medium in the ordinary manner by which the suspect would access it and downloading or displaying on the screen of the information processing device at the search location the suspect’s email-related electronic information stored there, this also concerns electronic information belonging to or possessed by the suspect, and therefore the seizure and search of that electronic information need not be viewed differently (see Supreme Court Decision 2017DO9747, decided 2017. 11. 29.). If, when voluntarily submitting a mobile phone, the suspect voluntarily provided the investigative agency with the ID and password for accessing cloud storage, etc., with the intent to submit to the investigative agency electronic information stored not in the mobile phone but in remote locations such as the cloud, managed by a third party, then the electronic information stored in the cloud, etc. may be regarded as having been voluntarily submitted.

B. Judgment

The court below는 its holding에서 든 이유로, Defendant가 자신의 voluntary intent에 기하여 possession하던 Samsung mobile phone Galaxy Note8을 investigative agency에 submitted하고, Galaxy Note8에 connected된 SDCard stored files, Naver Cloud files, and Galaxy Note gallery files를 investigative agency에 voluntarily submitted하였다고 판단하였다.

In light of the legal principles discussed above, the court below’s above determination is proper, and there is no error, as alleged in the grounds for final appeal, in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the unlawfulness of seizure procedures by voluntary submission, the admissibility of evidence voluntarily submitted, or the specification of the source of evidence, nor is there any error exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience.

4. Conclusion

Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and it is so adjudged as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2021DO11170]": "the grounds of appeal (상고이유서 제출기간이 지난 후에 제출된 상고이유보충서 기재는 적법한 상고이유를 보충하는 범위 내에서) are examined.

1. Regarding the Defendant’s grounds of appeal

A. Regarding the grounds of appeal challenging the admissibility of evidence

1) The evidence능력 of the electronic information stored in the two PCs in the lecturer break room of OO University (hereinafter, the PCs at issue)

a) Relevant legal principles

(1) Standards for determining the 압수범위 of electronic information and 관련성 where an information storage medium containing electronic information is voluntarily submitted

In light of the 중요성 of electronic information stored in an information storage medium, from the perspective of due process, the warrant principle, and the principle of proportionality that the Constitution and the Criminal Procedure Act seek to realize, as well as the protection of 사생활의 비밀과 자유, the right to informational self-determination, and property rights, a declaration of intent by a person voluntarily submitting an information storage medium to designate the electronic information contained therein or to limit the scope of submission must be strictly construed, and it is not permissible for an investigative agency to carelessly infer the unidentified submitter’s intent. Therefore, where an investigative agency can readily 확인 the submitter’s intent but, without doing so, voluntarily receives an information storage medium containing both electronic information related to a specific criminal suspicion and electronic information unrelated thereto, it cannot be treated as though all electronic information stored in that information storage medium was voluntarily submitted and seized.

When an investigative agency seeking to seize electronic information seizes an information storage medium and the electronic information stored therein by the method of voluntary submission, if, due to reasons such as failing to properly confirm the submitter’s intent regarding the specific scope of submission, the object and scope of the seizure of electronic information according to the voluntary submission are unclear or cannot be ascertained, only electronic information related to the criminal suspicion that motivated the seizure pursuant to voluntary submission and having at least minimal value capable of proving it shall be subject to seizure. Here, electronic information related to the criminal suspicion may include not only the criminal suspicion itself or conduct directly related to an offense based on the same basic factual relationship, but also information that may be used as indirect or circumstantial evidence to prove the motive and background of the offense, the means and method of the offense, the time and place of the offense, and the like. However, such relevance is recognized only where, taken comprehensively in light of the content of the criminal suspicion that motivated the seizure pursuant to voluntary submission, the object of the investigation, the course of the investigation, the process of voluntary submission, and the like, there exists a concrete and individual nexus; mere similarity to the criminal suspicion or the fact that the offense is of the same kind is not sufficient to establish relevance (see, e.g., Supreme Court en banc Decision 2016DO348, decided November 18, 2021).

(2) Guarantee of the right to participate in the search, copying, and printing of electronic information

Where an investigative agency that has voluntarily received an information storage medium or a copy thereof containing both electronic information subject to seizure and electronic information not subject to seizure transfers the information storage medium, etc. to the prosecutor’s office or the like and searches, copies, and prints it, in such a series of processes it must, in principle, comply with the warrant requirement and due process by guaranteeing the opportunity to participate to the party subject to seizure/search under Articles 219 and 121 of the Criminal Procedure Act (hereinafter referred to as the person subject to seizure) or his or her defense counsel, by preparing and delivering a seizure inventory specifying the file details of the seized electronic information, and by taking appropriate measures to prevent arbitrary copying, etc. of electronic information unrelated to the criminal suspicion. If such measures were not taken, then, unless there are special circumstances such as where the person subject to seizure expressly indicated an intent not to participate or where, in light of the purpose and course of the voluntary submission or the nature and content of the process in which the act violating the procedure occurred, it cannot be deemed that the purpose of guaranteeing the opportunity to participate in the procedure to the person subject to seizure was substantially infringed, the seizure/search cannot be regarded as lawful, and this is not altered by the fact that the investigative agency copied or printed only electronic information related to the criminal suspicion from the information storage medium or its copy.

Furthermore, where a third party such as a victim voluntarily submits, without a warrant, an information storage medium belonging to or under the control of the suspect, it is difficult to deem that the suspect, who is the person substantially subject to seizure, consented to the investigative agency’s unrestricted search of all electronic information therein; moreover, even when the suspect himself or herself voluntarily submits the information, in view also of the fact that the suspect’s right to participate, etc. must be guaranteed, unless there are special circumstances, appropriate measures must be taken under Articles 219, 121, and 129 of the Criminal Procedure Act to guarantee the suspect’s procedural rights, such as guaranteeing the suspect the right to participate and delivering a list of the seized electronic information (see the above en banc decision in 2016DO348, etc.).

In this way, in addition to the person subject to seizure who voluntarily submitted the information storage medium, the information storage medium belonging to or under the control of the suspect as to which the right to participate must also be guaranteed to a suspect who is not the submitter refers to a case where the suspect, at the time of seizure/search or until a time temporally proximate thereto, actually dominated and managed the information storage medium, possessed and exercised exclusive authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information stored therein, and did not otherwise transfer or waive it to a third party according to his or her own intent, and thereby may be evaluated as the person substantially subject to seizure with respect to the electronic information stored in that information storage medium. Whether this applies must be determined not by a legal or ex post facto judgment based on the attribution of rights under civil law, but on the basis of the externally and objectively recognizable factual condition at the time of the seizure/search. Apart from such externally and objectively dominant and managerial conditions concerning the information storage medium, persons who merely had prior involvement in the use of the information storage medium or the creation/use of individual electronic information, or persons identified as the data subject by electronic information created in that process, are not to be treated as parties actually subjected to seizure/search.

b) Facts found

The reasons of the lower court judgment and the evidence lawfully admitted show the following facts.

(1) By around September 10, 2019, the prosecution had conducted investigative measures, including execution of search-and-seizure warrants for the Defendant’s professor’s research room at OO University and for ◇◇◇ High School, with criminal suspicion facts including forgery of a private document concerning a commendation certificate in the name of the President of OO University dated September 7, 2012 against the Defendant (the facts charged in Seoul Central District Court Case No. 2019GOHAP738), uttering of a forged private document arising from Person 1’s submission of the above commendation certificate in the application process to the Graduate School of Medicine of △△ University and □□ University, obstruction of the performance of official duties by deception concerning the admissions screening work of the Graduate School of Medicine of □□ University arising from the above commendation certificate and other false career entries, and other offenses related to Person 1’s fraudulent application to the medical graduate school.

(2) Person 2 had served as an assistant to the ☆☆ College of OO University from March 1, 2019, and had been responsible for taking over and managing the lecturer break room at OO University and the items therein from his or her predecessor. The PCs at issue were stored in the lecturer break room without any separate marking as to ownership or legal relations.

(3) The basic purport of Person 2’s statement regarding the ownership and management status of the PCs at issue was that, having been told by his or her predecessor that they were items left behind by retirees, so return them to the school authorities or handle them as appropriate, he or she understood them in that way. Furthermore, according to Person 2’s statement, if there were a professor who wished to use the PCs at issue, he or she intended to provide them.

(4) The Defendant’s side also argued, at the first hearing date in the first instance, that the Defendant had never used the PCs at issue and that they had been used only as shared PCs at OO University; although their arguments changed several times up to the lower court, their basic position was that the PCs at issue had been used as shared PCs at OO University, then taken by the Defendant to his or her residence, etc. for use for a certain period, and then returned to OO University around December 2016 so that they could again be used as shared PCs at the OO University English camp and the like. This is consistent with the state at the time of the search and seizure in this case, in which the objective and actual dominion, custody, and attribution of the authority to manage and dispose of the PCs at issue were with OO University.

(5) While cooperating in the investigation by guiding the prosecutorial investigators through the interior of the ☆☆ College building at OO University on September 10, 2019 based on the cooperation instructions of OO University, Person 2, at the request of the prosecutorial investigator, enabled the prosecutorial investigator to operate one of the PCs at issue and to inspect the electronic information stored therein. In the course of the prosecutorial investigator’s search of the electronic information stored in that PC in Person 2’s presence, a folder related to Person 3 was discovered, and while the search continued, a situation occurred in which the PC emitted a pop sound and powered off. Thereupon, the prosecutorial investigator asked Person 2 and Person 4, the Director of the Administrative Support Office who oversaw the management of OO University’s property, whether they could discontinue the search at the scene and submit the PCs at issue to the prosecution.

(6) In response, Person 2 and Person 4 voluntarily submitted the PCs at issue in response to the prosecutorial investigator’s request, and in that process they entered their personal details, signed, and affixed their seals/thumbprints on the Consent to Voluntary Submission form, which stated that they were voluntarily submitting the PCs at issue and listed the PCs at issue in the section for voluntarily submitted items.

(7) At that time, the prosecutorial investigator asked Person 2 and Person 4 whether they wished to attend the imaging and search of the PCs at issue, extraction of electronic information, and the like, but Person 2 and Person 4 replied that they would not attend. Thereafter, Person 2 and Person 4 entered their personal details, signed, and affixed their seals/thumbprints in the section for the person subject to seizure, voluntary submitter, of the Confirmation of Whether to Attend the Submission and Imaging, etc. of an Information Storage Medium form (hereinafter referred to as the Confirmation of Whether to Attend), which stated in substance that they would not attend the hard copy, imaging, search and copying printing of electronic information, and the like.

(8) The prosecutorial investigator received the above Consent to Voluntary Submission and Confirmation of Whether to Attend from Person 2 and Person 4, delivered to them a Seizure Inventory Receipt concerning the PCs at issue, and then took the PCs at issue to the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office. In that process, the prosecutorial investigator did not additionally reconfirm with Person 2 and Person 4 their intent regarding the specific scope of submission of the electronic information stored in the PCs at issue.

(9) Thereafter, the prosecution carried out imaging and forensic work on the PCs at issue to extract electronic information, and as a result, evidence was discovered indicating that the forgery of the private document concerning the commendation certificate in the name of the President of OO University had been carried out around June 16, 2013 using one of the PCs at issue.

(10) Accordingly, on November 27, 2019, in Seoul Central District Court Case No. 2019GOHAP738, the prosecution filed a motion for amendment of the indictment, changing the existing charged facts that the Defendant forged a commendation certificate in the name of the President of OO University by arbitrarily affixing the President’s official seal of OO University on September 7, 2012 at OO University to the effect that the Defendant forged a commendation certificate in the name of the President of OO University in electronic file form using a PC at his or her residence on June 16, 2013. However, upon being denied leave on the ground that the identity of the charged facts was not recognized, the prosecution additionally indicted the Defendant on December 17, 2019 in Seoul Central District Court Case No. 2019GOHAP1050 on charged facts identical to those in the motion for amendment of the indictment.

(11) On February 11, 2020, the prosecution delivered to Person 2 and Person 4 a list specifying the file details of the electronic information extracted from and seized from the PCs at issue.

(12) The electronic information stored in the PCs at issue was used as evidence of the offenses related to Person 1’s fraudulent application to the medical graduate school among the facts charged in this case, including forgery of a private document dated June 16, 2013 (the facts charged in Seoul Central District Court Case No. 2019GOHAP1050).

c) Holding

(1) Voluntary submission of the PCs at issue

In light of the foregoing legal principles, examination of the above facts found shows that, as of September 10, 2019, the PCs at issue were not being used exclusively by a specific person for a specific purpose, but were being kept in the lecturer break room for nearly three years on the premise that OO University personnel would use them as shared PCs at OO University or otherwise dispose of them at their discretion, and the assistant responsible for the management and custody of the PCs at issue at the ☆☆ College of OO University, Person 2, was carrying out the custody and management duties concerning the PCs at issue. It is therefore recognized that Person 2, the assistant in charge of the custody and management duties at the time, and Person 4, the Director of the Administrative Support Office overseeing the management of OO University’s property, submitted the PCs at issue to the prosecution according to a voluntary intent reflecting OO University’s position.

(2) Necessity and relevance of the seizure of electronic information stored in the PCs at issue

(a) In light of the foregoing legal principles, the lower court erred in presuming that, in the case of a voluntary submission of an information storage medium and the electronic information stored therein, the object of seizure is not limited to the extent that necessity and relevance are recognized, and in concluding that, even though the investigative agency did not confirm with Person 2 and Person 4 their intent regarding the specific scope of submission of the electronic information stored in the PCs at issue, all of the PCs at issue and all electronic information stored therein could be regarded as having been voluntarily submitted. The PCs at issue were an information storage medium in which electronic information related to the criminal suspicion concerning the Defendant and electronic information unrelated thereto were commingled, and in such a case, it is in principle impermissible to arbitrarily infer the unidentified submitter’s intent and treat all electronic information stored in the PCs as having been voluntarily submitted and seized.

(b) Where, as such, the object and scope of seizure of electronic information according to the voluntary submitter’s intent cannot be clearly ascertained, only electronic information related to the criminal suspicion that motivated the seizure pursuant to the voluntary submission and having at least minimal value capable of proving it should be deemed subject to seizure.

At the time of the voluntary submission of the PCs at issue, the Defendant was already under investigation for the offense of uttering a forged private document to the effect that a forged commendation certificate in the name of the President of OO University had been submitted in the application process to the Graduate School of Medicine of △△ University and □□ University by Person 1, as well as for obstruction of the performance of official duties by deception concerning the admissions screening work of the Graduate School of Medicine of □□ University arising from the above commendation certificate and other false career entries.

Accordingly, electronic information created by using the PCs at issue in the process of Person 1’s fraudulent application to the medical graduate school, such as the Defendant’s use of one of the PCs at issue on June 16, 2013 to forge the above commendation certificate, can be regarded as evidence having a concrete and individual nexus to proving the motive and background, means and method, and the like, of the offense concerning the above criminal suspicion, and even comprehensively considering the object and course of this investigation and the process of voluntary submission, it is sufficient to recognize necessity and relevance.

(c) Ultimately, among the electronic information stored in the PCs at issue, the portions used as evidence of the offenses related to Person 1’s fraudulent application to the medical graduate school among the facts charged in this case have both necessity and relevance for seizure pursuant to voluntary submission; thus, the lower court’s legal error as noted above does not affect the result of the judgment.

(3) Guarantee of the right to participate in the process of search and extraction of the electronic information stored in the PCs at issue

(a) In light of the foregoing legal principles, the lower court erred in stating, in substance, that when an information storage medium and the electronic information stored therein are voluntarily submitted and seized, there is in principle no room to recognize the right to participate on the part of the person subject to seizure or the suspect during the process of searching the electronic information.

The PCs at issue were an information storage medium in which electronic information related to the criminal suspicion concerning the Defendant and electronic information unrelated thereto were commingled, and after the prosecution voluntarily received them from Person 2 and Person 4 and seized them, the prosecution moved them to the National Digital Forensics Center of the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office and, in the process of searching and extracting the electronic information stored therein, had, in principle, to guarantee the opportunity to participate to OO University, the person subject to seizure.

(b) However, as seen in the facts found above, in light of the course of the search and extraction of the electronic information related to the criminal suspicion from the PCs at issue, it is recognized that the prosecution confirmed the intent to participate and afforded an opportunity to Person 2 and Person 4, who were the persons subject to seizure, but that the persons subject to seizure waived that opportunity. Therefore, it cannot be said that there was a defect in the seizure/search procedure for the electronic information extracted from the PCs at issue in that the right to participate of the persons subject to seizure was not guaranteed.

Furthermore, in light of the purpose of guaranteeing the opportunity for the persons subject to seizure to participate as one of the appropriate measures to prevent distortion of electronic information in an information storage medium subject to seizure/search or arbitrary copying of electronic information unrelated to the suspected facts (see Supreme Court Order 2009MO1190, dated May 26, 2011, Supreme Court en banc Order 2011MO1839, dated July 16, 2015, etc.), examining the entire process of the seizure/search in this case, the reasons asserted by the Defendant alone, such as that no additional measure such as detailed notification of the criminal suspicion facts was taken with respect to Person 2 at the time of seizure pursuant to voluntary submission of the PCs at issue, cannot establish that the purpose of guaranteeing procedural participation to the persons subject to seizure was substantially infringed.

(c) Also, examining the above facts found on the basis of the foregoing legal principles, when viewed according to the objectively and externally recognizable factual condition at the time of the seizure/search pursuant to voluntary submission of the PCs at issue, it cannot be recognized that the PCs at issue or the electronic information stored therein belonged to or were under the Defendant’s ownership or control. Rather, in light of objective circumstances such as OO University’s actual domination and management of the PCs at issue by keeping them in the lecturer break room for nearly three years from around December 2016 while also seeming to be able to use them as shared PCs or take other measures such as discretionary disposal, it is recognized that OO University was, at that time, in a state of actually possessing and exercising comprehensive authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information stored in the PCs at issue.

Even considering all the circumstances asserted by the Defendant, such as that the Defendant had, before around December 2016, taken the PCs at issue to the Defendant’s residence, etc. and used them exclusively, or that after around December 2016 the lecturer break room where the PCs at issue were stored was near the Defendant’s professor’s research room, it cannot be said that the Defendant’s actual domination and management of the PCs at issue and the authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information stored therein continued until the time of the seizure/search in this case. Accordingly, this case does not fall within a situation in which the Defendant can be evaluated as the person substantially subject to seizure/search in relation to the seizure/search in this case.

Therefore, even under the legal principles set forth in the above Supreme Court en banc Decision 2016DO348, the seizure/search of the electronic information stored in the PCs at issue does not fall within a case in which the suspect’s right to participate must be guaranteed.

(d) Meanwhile, the Defendant also argues that, during the seizure/search process of the electronic information stored in the PCs at issue, the Defendant’s side should have been guaranteed the right to participate on the ground that the Defendant’s side was the data subject of the electronic information. As noted above, in order for a suspect to assert a right to participate in the course of searching electronic information in an information storage medium voluntarily submitted without the suspect’s involvement, the premise is the suspect’s actual domination and control over the information storage medium and possession of exclusive authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information therein. Therefore, this argument cannot be accepted, as it is not intended to recognize the right to participate even to those who merely participated in the creation or use of individual electronic information, or to persons who are the data subjects identified by the electronic information created in that process, irrespective of such domination and control.

(e) Ultimately, the right to participate was guaranteed to the persons subject to seizure in the course of the search and extraction of the electronic information stored in the PCs at issue, and the case does not fall within a situation where the Defendant’s side also had to be guaranteed a right to participate; accordingly, the lower court’s error in this part also does not affect the result of the judgment.

(4) Admissibility of the electronic information extracted from the PCs at issue

The lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, held that the prosecution’s voluntary receipt and seizure of the PCs at issue from OO University, the possessor and custodian of those PCs, did not constitute an unlawful investigation after indictment, that it could not be said that the admissibility of the electronic information extracted from the PCs at issue was recognized only if the Defendant’s side consented thereto, and that the electronic information extracted from the PCs at issue could be used as evidence because the identity and integrity between that electronic information, the documents printed therefrom, and the originals were proven.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the foregoing legal principles and the facts found above, although there are some inappropriate parts in the lower court’s statement of reasons, the conclusion of the lower court recognizing the admissibility of the evidence extracted from the PCs at issue is proper, and there is no error affecting the judgment, such as misapprehension of legal principles concerning compulsory investigation after indictment, the necessity of consent of the data subject in the seizure/search of voluntarily submitted items by a third party’s consent, the status and voluntariness of the custodian in seizure of voluntarily submitted items, the scope of the provisions mutatis mutandis of Article 219 of the Criminal Procedure Act in the seizure of voluntarily submitted items from an information storage medium, identity and integrity with the original, and the warrant requirement, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

2) Admissibility of the results of execution of the search-and-seizure warrants for tracing financial accounts

a) The lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, held that, in executing the search-and-seizure warrants for tracing financial accounts, the prosecution’s series of execution methods—sending, through the Criminal Justice Information Network, requests for provision of financial transaction information, copies of the warrants, and copies of the investigators’ identification cards to several financial institutions by electronic fax, receiving financial transaction data by e-mail or fax from the financial institutions, analyzing the received financial transaction data, then finally preparing a list of selected data related to the case, and thereafter directly visiting the financial institutions to present the original warrants, storing the selected data in a storage medium, while also delivering a seizure inventory and preparing a seizure protocol—did not violate the seizure/search procedures prescribed by the Constitution and the Criminal Procedure Act, and that the financial transaction data collected and submitted as evidence by such method in this case were admissible.

b) However, as a matter of principle, investigative agencies’ seizure and search must be based on a search-and-seizure warrant issued by a judge, and the original warrant must be presented to the person receiving the disposition (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2015DO10648, decided September 7, 2017; Supreme Court Decision 2018DO2841, decided March 14, 2019). Accordingly, even in executing a search-and-seizure warrant for tracing financial accounts, if the investigative agency did not present the original warrant in advance to the financial institution before receiving financial transaction data from it, such method cannot in principle be regarded as a lawful method of execution.

However, where, as a result of the investigative agency’s request to the financial institution for provision of financial transaction information under Article 4(2) of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Secrecy (hereinafter, the Financial Real Name Act), accompanied by a copy of the warrant, the financial transaction data received in reply from the financial institution fall within the objects and scope of execution of the warrant; and where the entire process of requesting provision of financial transaction information and receiving the data by facsimile transmission or electronic transmission is based on the financial institution’s voluntary willingness to cooperate; and where, after going through the procedure of selecting from among the data those financial transactions related to the criminal suspicion facts, the original warrant is finally presented and the seizure procedure is executed for the financial transaction data thus selected; and where the process is carried out in the manner prescribed by the Financial Real Name Act and there are no circumstances suggesting that it was otherwise conducted with the intent to circumvent due process and the warrant requirement—only in such a case may it exceptionally be regarded as a lawful method of execution of the warrant, on the basis that the entire series of procedures can be evaluated as presenting the original warrant in a timely manner based on one warrant and seizing or searching on that basis.

c) In light of such legal principles, examining the process of execution of each of the search-and-seizure warrants for tracing financial accounts in this case, even if the original warrant was not presented in advance to the financial institution before the investigative agency received financial transaction data from it, this case falls within a situation where the subsequent series of procedures—after going through the selection process for data related to the criminal suspicion facts, ultimately presenting the original warrant and directly seizing the selected data—can, viewed as a whole, be evaluated as presenting the original warrant in a timely manner based on one warrant and seizing or searching within the original objects and scope of execution of the warrant on that basis. Nor are there circumstances sufficient to recognize that the investigative agency executed the warrant in the above manner with the intent to circumvent due process and the warrant requirement.

Accordingly, the lower court’s conclusion that the admissibility of the financial transaction data secured in the execution process of the search-and-seizure warrants for tracing financial accounts in this case is recognized is proper, and there is no error affecting the judgment, such as misapprehension of legal principles concerning the method of presenting the warrant and the lawfulness of the seizure/search procedure, the admissibility of the seized items and secondary evidence in this part, or insufficient judicial examination, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

3) 120,000 physical shares of [Company Name 1 omitted]

The lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, held that the search-and-seizure warrant concerning 120,000 physical shares of [Company Name 1 omitted] was lawfully presented to the person subject to seizure, and that admissibility of evidence was recognized because the necessity of seizure and relevance to the criminal suspicion facts were also recognized.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error, such as misapprehension of legal principles concerning the admissibility of evidence of this seized item and secondary evidence, or insufficient judicial examination, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

4) Admissibility of the audio recording file of a telephone conversation kept by [Company Name 2 omitted]

The lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, held that the necessity of seizure and the relevance to the criminal suspicion facts were recognized with respect to the audio recording file of the telephone conversation kept by [Company Name 2 omitted], and thus the evidence was admissible.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error, such as misapprehension of legal principles concerning the admissibility of evidence of this seized item and secondary evidence, or insufficient judicial examination, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

B. Regarding the grounds of appeal concerning the offenses related to Person 1’s fraudulent application to the medical graduate school

For the reasons stated in its judgment, the lower court found that the Defendant forged the commendation certificate in the name of the President of OO University as alleged in the facts charged in this part (업무방해, 위계공무집행방해, the forged official document offense concerning the experiential activity confirmation issued in the name of the head of the ◎◎◎◎ Research Institute of ▽▽ University, the alternative charge of forged official document offense concerning the internship confirmation issued in the name of the head of the ▷▷▷▷▷ Center of ◁ University at △△ University, forgery of a private document dated June 16, 2013, and uttering of a forged private document), and that all other supporting documents were also false; that submitting them in the application process to the Graduate School of Medicine of △△ University and □□ University by Person 1, or entering them in the career history, constituted deception for the offenses of 업무방해 and 위계공무집행방해; that the Defendant’s intent and the conspiracy with Person 1, etc. were recognized in that process; and that this constituted an act obstructing the admissions screening work of each medical graduate school and could not be regarded as merely due to inadequate review by the persons in charge. On that basis, the lower court found this part of the charges guilty.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error affecting the judgment, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, misapprehension of legal principles concerning the establishment of co-principal liability, the deception and intent elements of 업무방해 and 위계공무집행방해, or danger of obstruction, or omission of judgment or insufficient judicial examination, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

C. Regarding the grounds of appeal concerning the fraud and violation of the former Subsidy Management Act (the Act before amendment by Act No. 13931 on January 28, 2016; hereinafter, the former Subsidy Act)

For the reasons stated in its judgment, the lower court held that the special grant money stated in the facts charged in this part constituted a subsidy under the former Subsidy Act, and that the Defendant fraudulently applied for and received research assistant allowances, thereby finding that this constituted a deceptive act for the offense of fraud. On that basis, the lower court found this part of the charges guilty.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error affecting the judgment, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehension of legal principles concerning the interpretation of Article 2(1) and Article 9 of the former Subsidy Act, Article 4(1) [Appended Table 1] of the Enforcement Decree of the same Act, or deception in the offense of fraud, or insufficient judicial examination, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

D. Regarding the grounds of appeal concerning the part violating the Capital Markets and Financial Investment Services Act (hereinafter, the Capital Markets Act) due to the use of undisclosed material information, excluding the part acquitted on grounds

The lower court, for the reasons stated in its judgment, held that, as alleged in the facts charged in this part, the Defendant purchased shares of [Company Name 1 omitted] using undisclosed material information. On that basis, the lower court found this part of the charges guilty.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error affecting the judgment, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehension of legal principles concerning the establishment of the act of using undisclosed material information, the presumption of innocence, insufficient judicial examination, or lack of reasons, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

E. Regarding the grounds of appeal concerning the part violating the Financial Real Name Act, excluding the part acquitted

For the reasons stated in its judgment, the lower court held that the Defendant borrowed the accounts stated in the facts charged in this part for the purpose of evading the law and conducted financial transactions for his or her own account, thereby finding that this part of the charges was proven. On that basis, the lower court found this part of the charges guilty.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error affecting the judgment, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehension of legal principles concerning the purpose of evading the law in the offense of violating the Financial Real Name Act, or insufficient judicial examination, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

F. Regarding the grounds of appeal concerning instigation of destruction of evidence

For the reasons stated in its judgment, the lower court held that the Defendant, as alleged in the facts charged in this part, with the intent to destroy materials related to Person 3 or materials related to Person 5, who were evidence in the Defendant’s criminal case, conspired with Person 6 and Person 7 to cause instigation of destruction of evidence against employees of [Company Name 3 omitted], and that common intent to act jointly and functional control over the act were recognized, and that such conduct by the Defendant constituted an abuse of the right of defense. On that basis, the lower court found this part of the charges guilty.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error affecting the judgment, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehension of legal principles concerning the establishment of co-principal liability for instigation of destruction of evidence, the intent to instigate and common intent to act jointly regarding the instigation, the evidence relating to a criminal case or disciplinary case under the offense of destruction of evidence, or abuse of the right of defense, or contradiction in reasons, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

G. Regarding the grounds of appeal concerning instigation of concealment of evidence

For the reasons stated in its judgment, the lower court found that the Defendant instructed Person 8 to conceal evidence concerning the storage medium of the PC at the Defendant’s residence and the main unit of the PC in the Defendant’s professor’s research room at OO University, as alleged in the facts charged in this part; that such conduct by the Defendant constituted instigation, not co-principal liability for concealment of evidence; and that Person 8 merely resolved to conceal evidence in accordance with the Defendant’s instructions and common intent to act jointly could not be recognized. On that basis, the lower court reversed the first-instance judgment, which had found this part of the charges not guilty, and found the Defendant guilty.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence lawfully admitted, the lower court’s determination contains no error affecting the judgment, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehending the legal principles concerning recognition of consummation and principal offender in the offense of concealment of evidence, the functional control over the act that serves as the criterion for distinguishing co-principal liability from instigation liability, the commencement of execution of concealment of evidence, or Person 8’s common intent to act jointly, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

2. Regarding the Prosecutor’s grounds of appeal

For the reasons stated in its judgment, the lower court maintained the first-instance judgment insofar as it found not proven or declared not guilty, with respect to the principal charges concerning uttering of a forged official document, embezzlement in the course of duties, violation of the Capital Markets Act due to the use of undisclosed material information in connection with over-the-counter purchase of 120,000 physical shares of [Company Name 1 omitted], and violation of the Act on the Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment, violation of the Capital Markets Act due to a false report of change, violation of the Financial Real Name Act by using the account of [Company Name 2 omitted] (account number omitted), and instigation of evidence forgery, among the facts charged in this case, concerning the internship confirmation issued in the name of the head of the ▷▷▷▷▷ Center of ◁ University at △△ University.

Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the lower court’s determination contains no error affecting the judgment, such as exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehension of legal principles concerning the intent for the offense of uttering a forged official document, the intent of unlawful appropriation for the offense of embezzlement in the course of duties, the establishment of the offense of violating the Capital Markets Act due to the use of undisclosed material information, the establishment of co-principal liability, the purpose of evading the law in the offense of violating the Financial Real Name Act, or misapprehension of legal principles concerning instigating conduct, or omission of judgment, as argued in the grounds of appeal.

3. Conclusion

Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated, as stated in the order."}

{"[2022DO7453]": "We examine 상고이유를 판단한다.

1. Determination of the argument that the legal doctrine concerning the right to participate in the voluntary submission procedure for a digital storage medium was misunderstood

가. Relevant legal principles

1) 정보저장매체 내 전자정보의 중요성은 Constitution과 Criminal Procedure Act가 구현하고자 하는 due process, warrant requirement, proportionality 원칙과 함께 사생활의 비밀과 자유, 정보에 대한 자기결정권의 관점에서 나온다.

When a law-enforcement agency, having received a digital storage medium or its duplicate by voluntary submission, where seized electronic information and non-seized electronic information are intermingled, carries the medium to the office and searches, copies, and prints it, the agency must in that series of processes guarantee participation to the party subject to seizure and search under Articles 219 and 121 of the Criminal Procedure Act, or to that person’s defense counsel, prepare and deliver a seizure inventory specifying the file details of the seized electronic information, and take appropriate measures to prevent arbitrary copying of electronic information unrelated to the suspected crime facts, thereby complying with the warrant requirement and due process. If such measures were not taken, then unless there are special circumstances such as the party subject to seizure side expressly indicating no intention to participate, or the purpose and course of the voluntary submission or the nature and content of the process in which the violation occurred making it impossible to say that the participation-guarantee purpose was substantially infringed, the seizure and search cannot be regarded as lawful; nor does it matter even if the agency copied and printed only electronic information related to the suspected crime facts from the digital storage medium or its duplicate.

Where a victim or other third party voluntarily submits a digital storage medium belonging to or under the control of the suspect, it is difficult to regard the substantive person subject to seizure, that is, the suspect, as having consented to the law-enforcement agency’s unrestricted search of all electronic information, and even compared with the case where the suspect himself or herself makes the voluntary submission, in which participation right and related rights must be guaranteed unless special circumstances exist, appropriate measures to secure procedural rights such as guaranteeing participation and delivering an inventory of seized electronic information must be taken, see Supreme Court en banc decision of November 18, 2021, 2016DO348, etc.

2) The digital storage medium belonging to or under the control of the suspect, to which participation right must be guaranteed not only for the person subject to seizure who voluntarily submitted it but also for the suspect who is not the volunteer submitter, means a case where the suspect, at the time of seizure and search or at a temporally close point thereto, actually dominates and controls the medium while retaining and exercising exclusive authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information stored therein, and has not otherwise transferred or abandoned it to a third party according to his or her own will, so that the suspect can be evaluated as a substantive party to the seizure and search as to all electronic information stored in the medium. Whether this applies is to be determined not by a legal judgment based on civil-law attribution of rights, but by the factual condition outwardly and objectively recognizable at the time of seizure and search. Apart from such outward and objective state of domination and control, it is not enough to treat someone as a substantive party subject to seizure and search merely because the suspect or another third party had in the past been involved in the use of the medium or in the creation or use of individual electronic information, or because they correspond to the data subject identified by electronic information created in that process, see Supreme Court decision of January 27, 2022, 2021DO11170, etc.

나. Facts found

According to the reasons of the lower-court judgment and the evidence duly admitted, the following facts can be found.

1) The law-enforcement agency, starting with the seizure and search conducted around August 27, 2019, on (Name 2 omitted) University, (Name 3 omitted) office, and (Name 1 omitted) academy, etc. in connection with suspicions of admissions and academic irregularities involving the children of Non-Indicted Persons 1 and 2, suspicions of improprieties in private equity fund investments, suspicions of irregularities at the (Name 1 omitted) academy, and the like, began a full-scale investigation into the various allegations.

2) In preparation for the investigation such as seizure and search, Non-Indicted Person 1, in order to conceal computers storing electronic information related to the suspected facts, around August 31, 2019, handed over to Non-Indicted Person 3 three digital storage media used by Non-Indicted Persons 1, etc. at their residence, namely one of two digital storage media detached from a computer in the study, two digital storage media detached from the computer of his son Non-Indicted Person 4, and instructed him to hide them until the investigation is over. Non-Indicted Person 3 concealed the instant hard disk drive in places such as a personal locker at a gym on the basement level 1 of a commercial building located in Yangcheon-gu, Seoul.

3) The instant hard disk drive stored evidence that Non-Indicted Person 1 intended to conceal, namely internship certificates used in his children’s university and graduate school admissions and text messages of Non-Indicted Person 4, the Defendant, and other related persons.

4) The law-enforcement agency, around September 10, 2019, took Non-Indicted Person 3 into custody as a suspect on charges of concealment of evidence. Non-Indicted Person 3 voluntarily submitted the instant hard disk drive to the law-enforcement agency on September 11, 2019.

5) In the process of the voluntary submission of the instant hard disk drive and the search, copying, and printing of the electronic information stored therein, the law-enforcement agency guaranteed the participation right by confirming with Non-Indicted Person 3 and his defense counsel whether they wished to participate and by affording them the opportunity to participate, but Non-Indicted Person 3’s side indicated an intention not to participate in the search, copying, and printing process. The law-enforcement agency did not confirm such intention to participate with Non-Indicted Persons 1, etc. nor afford them an opportunity to participate.

다. Determination

Taking into account the legal principles examined above and the following circumstances discernible from the above facts found, it cannot be said that participation rights must be guaranteed also to Non-Indicted Persons 1, etc., who were not the persons making the voluntary submission, in addition to Non-Indicted Person 3, who voluntarily submitted the instant hard disk drive as a suspect in the offense of concealment of evidence. In the same purport, the lower court’s determination recognizing the admissibility of the electronic information stored in the instant hard disk drive is justified and can be accepted.

1) Non-Indicted Person 3, as a suspect in the offense of concealment of evidence, which was the criminal facts giving rise to the voluntary submission, voluntarily submitted the instant hard disk drive during the investigation against him. The instant hard disk drive and the electronic information stored therein are evidence not only concerning the suspected facts of Non-Indicted Persons 1, etc., who are the principal offenders, but also the direct object of the concealment act, and thus constitute evidence concerning Non-Indicted Person 3’s suspicion of concealment of evidence. Accordingly, Non-Indicted Person 3 is a person with a substantive interest in the instant hard disk drive and the electronic information stored therein. Throughout the entire process, including the voluntary submission of the medium itself and the searching, copying, and printing of the electronic information related to the suspicion of concealment of evidence, Non-Indicted Person 3 has an interest in participation.

2) As the investigation into himself and Non-Indicted Persons 2, etc. became full-scale, Non-Indicted Person 1 delivered the instant hard disk drive to Non-Indicted Person 3 while instructing him to hide it. Non-Indicted Person 3 voluntarily concealed the instant hard disk drive in a place known only to himself so that it would not be discovered. Thereafter, when Non-Indicted Person 3 was taken into custody as a suspect on suspicion of concealment of evidence, he disclosed the concealment to the law-enforcement agency and voluntarily submitted the instant hard disk drive. In light of the circumstances surrounding the concealment and voluntary submission, and the extent of involvement of Non-Indicted Person 3 and Non-Indicted Persons 1, etc. in that process, it may be said that the person who actually possessed the instant hard disk drive at the time of seizure and search or at a time close thereto was Non-Indicted Person 3. Further, insofar as Non-Indicted Person 3 actually possessed the instant hard disk drive around that time by the foregoing circumstances, it may be regarded, absent other special circumstances, that he was also in a position to de facto retain and exercise authority to manage and dispose of the stored electronic information.

3) Non-Indicted Person 1 was not the suspect in the offense of concealment of evidence, which was the criminal facts giving rise to the voluntary submission, and moreover, he delivered the instant hard disk drive to Non-Indicted Person 3, requesting vaguely that it be hidden until the investigation into himself is over, with the purpose of concealing the very existence of the instant hard disk drive. This can be regarded as an expression of an intention, under the purpose of concealing and severing the outward connection between himself and the instant hard disk drive and the electronic information stored therein, to abandon or wholly transfer to Non-Indicted Person 3 the exclusive right of domination and control over the instant hard disk drive until the indefinite time of completion of the investigation, if necessary for achieving that purpose. As a result, Non-Indicted Person 3 came to be in a state where he could de facto retain and exercise actual and factual domination over the instant hard disk drive and exclusive authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information stored therein, and he actually exercised that authority by concealing the medium at a place of his own choosing and thereafter voluntarily submitting it to the law-enforcement agency.

2. Determination of the remaining arguments for final appeal

The lower court maintained the first-instance judgment, which found the facts charged in this case guilty for the reasons stated in the opinion. Examining the reasons of the lower-court judgment in light of the relevant legal principles and the evidence duly admitted, there is no error affecting the judgment in that the lower court either exceeded the limits of free evaluation of evidence by violating the rules of logic and experience, without fully conducting the necessary examination, or misunderstood the legal principles concerning relevance between the seized items and the facts charged, abuse of prosecutorial authority, the presumption of innocence and the principle of trial based on evidence concerning the falsity of the instant certificate, deception and risk of result in the crime of obstruction of business, intent and co-principal liability, and the admissibility of derivative evidence, etc.

3. Conclusion

Therefore, the final appeal is dismissed, and judgment is rendered as stated in the main text. In this judgment, except for the dissenting opinion of Supreme Court Justices Min Yu-sook, Lee Heung-gu, and Oh Kyung-mi, the views of the participating Justices were unanimous, and there are the concurring opinions of Supreme Court Justices Ahn Cheol-sang, Noh Tae-ak, and Cheon Dae-yeop on the majority opinion, as well as the concurring opinion of Supreme Court Justice Oh Kyung-mi on the dissenting opinion.

4. Dissenting opinion of Supreme Court Justices Min Yu-sook, Lee Heung-gu, and Oh Kyung-mi

가. Summary of the dissenting opinion

1) The majority opinion held that Non-Indicted Person 3, who voluntarily submitted the instant hard disk drive, had a substantive interest in the electronic information stored therein as a suspect in the offense of concealment of evidence, and could de facto retain and exercise the authority to manage and dispose of that electronic information by actually possessing it; therefore, it was sufficient that participation rights were guaranteed to him in the seizure and search procedure, and since Non-Indicted Persons 1, etc., who handed over the instant hard disk drive to Non-Indicted Person 3 to conceal evidence concerning their own suspected facts, had abandoned or transferred the exclusive authority to manage and dispose of it, they did not correspond to the substantive persons subject to seizure who were the objects of the guarantee of participation rights.

2) However, we cannot agree. The majority opinion understands the substantive person subject to seizure, the subject to whom the participation right is guaranteed, narrowly with a focus on the suspect in the criminal facts that caused the seizure and search, and this does not accord with the purport and direction of the precedents. In addition, according to the majority opinion, by disregarding the constitutional demand to realize due process and the warrant requirement in the coercive disposition of the law-enforcement agency concerning electronic information, which is increasingly important to individuals and businesses in modern society, it allows an anti-constitutional result in which the fundamental rights concerning the secrecy and freedom of private life of the electronic-information manager and disposer, who is the substantive person subject to seizure, are infringed.

3) In the above Supreme Court en banc decision 2016DO348 and Supreme Court decision 2021DO11170, etc., the Supreme Court stated that the substantive person subject to seizure, who is the subject to whom participation rights are guaranteed in the seizure and search of electronic information, is a person who actually dominates and controls the digital storage medium concerned, retains and exercises exclusive authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information in that digital storage medium, and can be evaluated as a person who is a substantive party to the seizure and search thereof. According to the legal principles and purport of such precedents, where, in addition to the actual possessor and custodian of the digital storage medium, who is the direct party to the coercive disposition and the formal person subject to seizure, there separately exists an owner-manager, and there is a risk that his or her privacy and freedom, the right to informational self-determination, property rights, etc. concerning the electronic information may be infringed by the coercive disposition, that owner-manager must be regarded as the substantive person subject to seizure who is the object of the guarantee of participation rights. At this time, it is not required that the substantive person subject to seizure be the suspect in the criminal facts that caused the seizure and search.
